cases.input: An unchanged record moves to a new URL.
cases.expect: Record and version identity persist; only the location or instantiation changes.

cases.input: A migration creates a new format while all declared significant properties remain unchanged.
cases.expect: A new instantiation with provenance and digest remains attached to the same record version.

cases.input: A migration changes a declared significant content property.
cases.expect: A fixing event creates a new immutable record version without renumbering history.

cases.input: The same word appears in two distinct subject fields with different essential characteristics.
cases.expect: Distinct concept IRIs remain; lexical equality establishes no identity.

cases.input: Two authorities publish conflicting definitions for the same intension.
cases.expect: One concept may retain both sourced contextual definitions with language, status, access and dispute state.

cases.input: Two definitions use one label but differ in essential characteristics.
cases.expect: Distinct concepts are required and may be related only by an authorized mapping.

cases.input: A record classification identifies the subject, concept IRI, scheme IRI and exact release.
cases.expect: WM-XCT-020 owns a reproducible binding; any copied label is display-only.

cases.input: A concept exists before joining a scheme and is later withdrawn from one release.
cases.expect: Concept identity persists with zero memberships; entry and withdrawal remain release-local assertions.

cases.input: One scheme withdraws an active concept and the concept is later globally retired.
cases.expect: The local withdrawal and global tombstoned retirement remain separate events with separate masters.

cases.input: Different schemes prefer different designations for one concept.
cases.expect: The designation inventory stays concept-owned while each preference is owned by its pinned scheme release.

cases.input: A scheme publishes a scope note that narrows use without changing concept intension.
cases.expect: The scope note remains release-owned and cannot overwrite the intrinsic concept definition.

cases.input: A record is classified using only a display label.
cases.expect: The classification is rejected because concept, scheme and exact release pins are absent.

cases.input: Matching bytes are treated as proof that two records or concepts are identical.
cases.expect: The identity inference is rejected.

cases.input: Concept and scheme stores both edit the same membership or hierarchy assertion.
cases.expect: Validation rejects dual mastership and requires one release-owned assertion plus derived views.

cases.input: A retired concept identifier is silently repointed to a new meaning.
cases.expect: Validation rejects reuse and requires the original tombstone and an explicitly new identifier.

cases.input: A concept is merged or split after use in published releases.
cases.expect: New concept lifecycle assertions preserve old tombstones and identifiers; published release assertions remain immutable and successors pin new identities.

cases.input: A mapping relates concepts across two schemes.
cases.expect: One source-release-owned mapping assertion pins exact source and target releases; the target view is derived and read-only.

cases.input: A concept withdrawn in one release re-enters a later release.
cases.expect: Both release-local assertions remain append-only and concept identity stays unchanged.

cases.input: A definition is licensed for a restricted audience.
cases.expect: Concept identity remains visible as permitted while definition content obeys its own access scope.

cases.input: A stored instantiation digest no longer matches and the system silently rewrites it.
cases.expect: Validation rejects silent repair and requires an integrity event with retained prior evidence.

cases.input: A published scheme release is renumbered or its identifier is repointed.
cases.expect: Validation rejects mutation and requires an append-only successor release.

cases.input: A disputed definition automatically deprecates or redirects its concept.
cases.expect: Validation rejects the inference; dispute, deprecation and redirect are distinct.

cases.input: A superseded record or concept is destroyed solely because a successor exists.
cases.expect: Validation rejects destruction without separate retention and disposition authority.

cases.input: A scheme note contradicts the concept's intrinsic intension.
cases.expect: Validation rejects the note as a scope refinement and requires a distinct concept or governed correction.
